lab.intro: We are a research group in the School of Energy Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. Our work sits at the interface of nanofluidics and microfluidics: graphene-based desalination, streaming potential, nanofluidic channel fabrication, multiphase microfluidics, droplet dynamics, electrokinetics and the energy performance of buildings.
approach: Molecular dynamics of water, ions and polymers in nanoconfinement: slip, wettability and transport below a micron.
Experiments and simulations of electric double layers, droplets and multiphase flow in micro- and millichannels.
Solar thermal, wind and building energy systems, increasingly guided by machine learning.

pi.name: Dr. Chirodeep Bakli
pi.title: Associate Professor
roles: Chairperson, School of Energy Science & Engineering
awards: Associate, West Bengal Academy of Science and Technology
bio: My research focuses on multiscale fluid flow and heat transfer with the twin objectives to understand the interfacial interactions and flow physics, and to use them to develop smart surfaces and for renewable energy generation.

Part of the research focuses on length scales below micron dimensions, where one has to resort to molecular-level investigations. The results are used to propose a capillary-height-dependent dynamic slip length that explains the filling behaviour in nanocapillaries. For flow in confinement, the interfacial slip was shown to be a complex function of the physical and chemical signature of the solid surface and of the ionic inclusions in the solvent. In a pioneering work, the duality of wettability and slip length was challenged: flow on a hydrophobic surface was optimised to obtain stick, and methods were proposed to tune surface wettability by altering the structure of the solid and the fluid at the interface.

At the device level, theory and experiments decipher the interdependence between the structure of the electric double layer and the structure of the fluid at the interface under dynamic conditions, a road map for optimising electrokinetic energy conversion. At the system level, the research focuses on wind energy conversion and harvesting solar thermal energy.

themes.name: 2D Materials and Nanoconfinement
themes.short: Engineering solid–liquid interfaces at the nanoscale: wettability, slip and transport in graphene and carbon nanochannels.
themes.text: The science of manipulating solid–liquid interfaces at micro and nano sizes has great potential for a wide range of applications. By altering the surface chemistry or topography of solids, properties such as wettability and adhesion can be precisely adjusted, opening opportunities in self-cleaning coatings, microfluidic devices, wettability sensors, heat transfer, self-assembly, catalysis and thermal management. Starting from the smallest scale, the goal is to create long-lasting technologies that improve access to water and energy.

themes.name: Nanofluid Heat Transfer
themes.short: Nanoparticle suspensions, porous media and engineered heat sinks for better thermal management.
themes.text: Nanofluid heat transfer combines fluid dynamics and nanotechnology to transform thermal management. Dispersing nanoparticles in a base fluid such as water or oil raises thermal conductivity and improves convective transport, which enhances heat exchangers, radiators and cooling systems used in renewable energy generation and energy-efficient buildings. The group designs nanofluid compositions and heat-sink geometries that maximise heat transfer while minimising environmental impact.

themes.name: Fluid–Structure Interaction
themes.short: Coupled dynamics of deformable structures and the fluids around them, from flexible conduits to bio-inspired flows.
themes.text: Fluid–structure interaction (FSI) captures the two-way coupling between deformable structures and surrounding fluids, from fluttering flags to blood flow in arteries. Understanding this coupling is essential for optimising design, performance and structural integrity in aerospace, civil engineering, biomechanics and sustainable energy systems. The group combines computational methods, experiments and theory to study these interactions.

themes.name: Energy Studies of Buildings
themes.short: Passive cooling, phase-change materials, façades and green roofs for energy-efficient buildings.
themes.text: Buildings are a large share of energy demand. The group studies passive thermal management of buildings: phase-change materials integrated in direct-gain walls, machine-learning-guided façade optimisation, tree-shaped microchannel networks for passive cooling, hydrogel-based cooling, micro green roofing and district cooling with renewable energy integration.

themes.name: Interfacial Phenomena and Multiphase Microfluidics
themes.short: Immiscible phases in small channels: plugs, jets, mixing and core–annular flow.
themes.text: In multiphase microfluidics the interaction between immiscible phases controls a wide range of phenomena, from the adjustment of surface tension forces to the motion of droplets and bubbles. Precise control of fluid interfaces improves energy conversion and storage, and small channels allow effective blending, regulation of reactions and creation of materials.

themes.name: Droplet Dynamics
themes.short: Formation, impact, wetting and propulsion of droplets on engineered surfaces.
themes.text: Droplet dynamics examines how liquid droplets behave as they interact with their environment, shaped by surface tension, viscosity and external forces from formation to break-up, coalescence and impact. These processes matter for fuel combustion, spray cooling in power plants and water droplets on solar panels, and understanding them helps improve energy conversion and utilisation.

themes.name: Electrokinetics
themes.short: Electric fields, ions and flow at the micro- and nanoscale: streaming potential, energy conversion and translocation.
themes.text: Electrokinetics explores the interaction between electric fields and fluid flow. By manipulating electric charges it is possible to regulate the motion of fluids, colloids and particles at the micro- and nanoscale. The group studies electrophoresis, electroosmosis and streaming potential for electrokinetic energy conversion, desalination, ion rectification and biomolecule translocation.

join.text: We are always looking for enthusiastic young minds to join the lab. The group is currently looking for interns who are proficient in coding.
routes: Admission is through IIT Kharagpur's PhD admission process (School of Energy Science and Engineering). Write to Dr. Bakli with your CV and research interests before applying.
Openings on sponsored projects are advertised on IIT Kharagpur's temporary jobs page.
Students proficient in coding (simulation, data analysis, machine learning) are welcome to write in with a CV and a short note on what they would like to work on.
We welcome collaborations with academic and industry partners. Contact Dr. Bakli directly.
